title: Lerma v. Amazon.com Services, LLC et al., No. 8:22-cv-01727 (C.D. Cal.) — Class Action Complaint filed by Miguel Lerma, Jr., a registered California sex offender (PC §290), against Amazon.com Services, LLC, Amazon Logistics, Inc., and Accurate Background LLC, alleging Megan's Law (PC §290.46), Fair Chance Act (Gov. Code §12952), ICRAA, FCRA, and UCL violations arising from denial of a permanent Amazon Fresh store-associate position after a Mar. 2022 background check

Lerma v. Amazon — Judge Fred W. Slaughter GRANTS both defendants' motions to dismiss (Dkt. 36), DISMISSING WITHOUT PREJUDICE the Megan's Law, FCRA, and UCL claims. Critically, the court holds Accurate Background's own background report — subject to judicial notice — showed the disqualifying 2013 conviction information came from ordinary Orange County Superior Court criminal records, not the Megan's Law website; the report's National Sex Offender Database Search returned 'no record found.' The FCRA claim failed as entirely derivative of the rejected Megan's Law theory. Only the Fair Chance Act claim against Amazon (never challenged by either motion) survives

Lerma v. Amazon — Amazon answers the First Amended Complaint (Dkt. 45) as to the sole surviving claim: the Fair Chance Act claim, alleging Amazon failed to individually assess Lerma's decade-old conviction against the specific duties of the store-associate role despite having previously employed and praised him. Lerma never filed the Second Amended Complaint the May 26 order invited; the court had issued an Order to Show Cause re dismissal for lack of prosecution on Aug. 3, 2023

Lerma v.
